statement: Let (N, g, Q) be a smooth compact three-dimensional initial data set with boundary Γ− ⊔ Γ+. Assume Γ+ is nonempty and has positive expansion with its normal out of N. The inner part Γ− may be empty; when it is present, assume its expansion is negative with its normal into N. Consider all smooth domains whose inner boundary is Γ− and whose remaining boundary Σ lies in the interior of N and satisfies ΘQ(Σ) ≤ 0. They avoid Γ+, and their normal on Σ points out of the domain. If their union is nonempty, its closure has a smooth compact embedded stable MOTS frontier in the interior, separating it from Γ+. This closure is itself the closure of such a domain and contains every domain in the defining class. If Γ− is nonempty, the two strict barriers also give a nonempty smooth embedded enclosing MOTS.
